title: Questions at an izakaya
summary: Use question words to establish time, place, people, quantities, and preferences during a restaurant exchange.
takeaways: Question words stay in the normal sentence slot.
どちら compares two choices; どの must modify a noun.
Counters change shape, so learn them as answer patterns rather than isolated vocabulary.

grammar.title: Leave the unknown in place
grammar.pattern: Noun は Question word ですか
grammar.summary: Japanese does not move the question word to the front. Put いつ, どこ, だれ, or 何時 where the missing information belongs.

grammar.title: Compare two choices
grammar.pattern: A と B と どちらが …
grammar.summary: Use どちら for a polite choice between two things. The chosen thing is commonly marked by が with preference adjectives.

examples.english: Which do you like, sushi or tempura?

grammar.title: Choose within a noun category
grammar.summary: どの cannot stand alone; it must directly modify a noun such as size, color, or seat.
grammar.caution: どれ stands alone; どの always comes before a noun.

recall.prompt: Can どの stand by itself?
recall.answer: No. It must modify a noun.

recall.prompt: Where does a Japanese question word go?
recall.answer: In the same sentence position as the missing answer.
